spec.objective: Provide the injected live fetcher leaf exposing the Fetcher seam, an RSC:1 HTTP GET path for bulk feeds, and a Playwright path reserved for lazy-loaded per-disclosure detail bodies, all driveable by an injected stub so tests stay offline.
functional_requirements: Declare the seam Fetcher = Callable[[str, dict], tuple[int, str, dict]] (status, body, response-headers) at module scope so callers and tests can type/inject it.
fetch_hacktivity(fetcher: Fetcher) -> str issues an RSC: 1 header HTTP GET for the bulk hacktivity feed through the injected fetcher and returns the response body string.

fetch_repo_page(fetcher: Fetcher, owner: str, name: str) -> str returns the per-repo detail body via the injected fetcher, using the Playwright path only for lazy-loaded detail content and never performing form-fill or click.
spec.interfaces: Fetcher = Callable[[str, dict], tuple[int, str, dict]]; fetch_hacktivity(fetcher: Fetcher) -> str; fetch_repo_page(fetcher: Fetcher, owner: str, name: str) -> str
edge_cases: Fetcher returns a non-200 status (e.g. 429 or 503): the function surfaces/handles the failure deterministically rather than returning a silently-empty body.
Fetcher returns an empty or missing response-headers dict: body extraction still succeeds without raising KeyError.
non_goals: No real network I/O and no integration with live huntr endpoints in oracles; the stub fetcher is always injected.
NEVER auto-submit: no HTTP POST, no Playwright form-fill/click — findings are parked for a human only.
Do NOT re-derive JSON shapes or HTML parsing here, and do NOT retrofit ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py.

Mirror the seam style of ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py (Fetcher = Callable[[url, headers], (status, body, headers)]) and the runner-injection style of ngv2/acquisition/cloner.py. The RSC: 1 request header signals the bulk React Server Component feed; the Playwright branch only renders lazy detail bodies and must be bypassable via the injected fetcher so the oracle is hermetic.

```python
import pytest

from ngv2.sourcing.browser_fetcher import fetch_hacktivity, fetch_repo_page


class StubFetcher:
    def __init__(self, status=200, body="<html>ok</html>"):
        self.calls = []
        self.status = status
        self.body = body

    def __call__(self, url, headers):
        self.calls.append((url, dict(headers or {})))
        return (self.status, self.body, {"content-type": "text/x-component"})


def test_fetch_hacktivity_uses_rsc_header_and_returns_body():
    stub = StubFetcher(body="<html>feed</html>")
    body = fetch_hacktivity(stub)
    assert body == "<html>feed</html>"
    assert len(stub.calls) == 1
    url, headers = stub.calls[0]
    assert "huntr.com" in url and "/bounties/hacktivity" in url
    assert any(k.upper() == "RSC" and str(v) == "1" for k, v in headers.items())


def test_fetch_repo_page_targets_repo_path():
    stub = StubFetcher(body="<html>repo</html>")
    body = fetch_repo_page(stub, "alpha", "one")
    assert body == "<html>repo</html>"
    url, headers = stub.calls[0]
    assert "/repos/alpha/one" in url
    assert any(k.upper() == "RSC" and str(v) == "1" for k, v in headers.items())


# edge_case: non-200 response raises instead of returning a junk body
def test_non_200_raises():
    stub = StubFetcher(status=503, body="")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        fetch_hacktivity(stub)
    stub2 = StubFetcher(status=404, body="")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        fetch_repo_page(stub2, "alpha", "one")


# edge_case: fetcher seam is positional-compatible with huntr_client style
def test_fetcher_called_with_url_and_headers_mapping():
    stub = StubFetcher()
    fetch_hacktivity(stub)
    url, headers = stub.calls[0]
    assert isinstance(url, str) and isinstance(headers, dict)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# fetch_bounties_index — the /bounties eligibility index is SERVER-RENDERED
# HTML (its repo list is NOT in the RSC flight payload), so this fetch is a
# plain GET of https://huntr.com/bounties WITHOUT the RSC header.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
from ngv2.sourcing.browser_fetcher import fetch_bounties_index


def test_fetch_bounties_index_plain_get_no_rsc_header():
    stub = StubFetcher(body="<html>index</html>")
    body = fetch_bounties_index(stub)
    assert body == "<html>index</html>"
    url, headers = stub.calls[0]
    assert "huntr.com" in url and url.rstrip("/").endswith("/bounties")
    assert not any(k.upper() == "RSC" for k in headers)


# edge_case: non-200 on the index raises too
def test_fetch_bounties_index_non_200_raises():
    stub = StubFetcher(status=500, body="")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        fetch_bounties_index(stub)
```

acceptance_criteria: ngv2/sourcing/refresh_policy.py exposes is_stale(fetched_at, now, max_age_hours) -> bool and next_delay(attempt, base_seconds) -> float.
is_stale returns True only when (now - fetched_at) exceeds max_age_hours; equal/younger ages are fresh.
next_delay yields ~1 req/sec base politeness and grows with attempt for backoff.
The committed oracle tests/test_refresh_policy_wired.py passes against live ngv2.sourcing.refresh_policy.

spec.objective: Provide pure, side-effect-free staleness and polite rate-limit/backoff helpers over fetched_at timestamps so the entrypoint can decide whether to refetch and how long to wait between requests.
functional_requirements: is_stale(fetched_at: str, now: str, max_age_hours: float) -> bool returns True when the elapsed time between the two ISO timestamps exceeds max_age_hours, and False when the age is equal or younger.
next_delay(attempt: int, base_seconds: float) -> float returns a polite delay anchored at roughly base_seconds (~1 req/sec) for the first attempt and increasing for higher attempts to back off.

Do NOT build the learning/selection layer or any flock/file-lock side effects; the legacy rate_limiter flock pattern is read-only reference.

```python
"""RED oracle: ngv2/sourcing/refresh_policy.py — pure staleness + backoff.

Contract (from brief_hooks_live-fetch-and-refresh):
    is_stale(fetched_at: str, now: str, max_age_hours: float) -> bool
    next_delay(attempt: int, base_seconds: float) -> float

* Timestamps are ISO-8601 strings (the snapshot ``fetched_at`` format).
* ``is_stale`` is True when ``now - fetched_at`` exceeds ``max_age_hours``;
  a malformed/empty ``fetched_at`` is treated as stale (safe default).
* ``next_delay`` implements polite escalating backoff: at least
  ``base_seconds``, non-decreasing in ``attempt`` and growing for later
  attempts (rate-limit friendliness, ~1 req/sec base).
Pure: no clock reads — ``now`` is injected.
"""
from ngv2.sourcing.refresh_policy import is_stale, next_delay

T0 = "2026-06-12T00:00:00+00:00"
T0_PLUS_1H = "2026-06-12T01:00:00+00:00"
T0_PLUS_3H = "2026-06-12T03:00:00+00:00"


def test_fresh_snapshot_is_not_stale():
    assert is_stale(T0, T0_PLUS_1H, max_age_hours=2.0) is False


def test_old_snapshot_is_stale():
    assert is_stale(T0, T0_PLUS_3H, max_age_hours=2.0) is True


def test_equal_timestamps_are_fresh():
    assert is_stale(T0, T0, max_age_hours=1.0) is False


# edge_case: malformed/empty fetched_at counts as stale (safe default)
def test_malformed_fetched_at_is_stale():
    assert is_stale("not-a-timestamp", T0, max_age_hours=24.0) is True
    assert is_stale("", T0, max_age_hours=24.0) is True


# edge_case: backoff respects the base and never shrinks across attempts
def test_next_delay_monotonic_and_at_least_base():
    base = 1.0
    delays = [next_delay(attempt, base) for attempt in range(5)]
    assert all(d >= base for d in delays)
    assert all(b >= a for a, b in zip(delays, delays[1:]))
    assert delays[3] > delays[0]


def test_next_delay_scales_with_base():
    assert next_delay(2, 2.0) >= next_delay(2, 1.0)

```
